transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Tidewater HoS), Evan (Platform Eng), Lena (Compliance)
Shared links: Redwood SOC2 PDF (https://redwood.example/soc2.pdf), sample export doc (https://redwood.example/docs/admin-export), S3 export guide (link shared in chat)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intros — im Maya, AE on the infra team. Carlos is our security/infra systems engineer. Priya could you kick us off with what you want to cover?

[00:12] Priya (Tidewater): sure yeah thanks. main things, we need to understand exactly what admin activity is captured by Redwood, what fields are in those logs, how we can export them, and the options for encryption and key management. we have SOC2 and ISO audits incoming so we need the paper trail. also data residency — some logs need to stay in eu do we support region pinned exports?

[00:28] Maya: absolutely. at a high level we capture both user-facing request logs (api calls, model requests) and admin activity — things like user creation/role changes, policy updates, api key rotations, workspace exports, permission changes, and service-level actions like model rollout, failovers. Carlos will walk through the schema.

[00:43] Carlos (Redwood SE): yeah so the admin activity events are roughly: timestamp, actor (user id + email), action (create_user, change_role, grant_scope, revoke_key, kms_bind), target resource (workspace id, model id), request id / trace id, source ip, user-agent, outcome (success/failure), and optional metadata blob. We include session id when available and a KV cache reference for model ops — sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in older docs, sorry.

[01:15] Evan (Tidewater): that metadata blob, does it include payloads? like will it capture prompt text or PII?

[01:21] Carlos: good question. by default admin activity logs do not include full prompt bodies. operational traces for debug can include partial payloads but we mask sensitive fields by default. for retrievable artifacts there is an audit export feature that can include redact flags and a pointer to the actual artifact stored separately. we try to avoid storing raw customer prompt content in admin logs to limit PII exposure.

[01:45] Lena (Compliance): and retention policies — what are our options? we may need 7 years for certain regulatory evidence in specific regions. can you retain for that long?

[01:52] Maya: yes we support flexible retention tiers. hosted customers: default 90 days on hot storage, 1 year on warm, longer-term archive to cold (we can export to customer S3 or to Glacier) for multi-year retention. for enterprise / dedicated / private we provide configurable retention up to 7+ years depending on contract.

[02:12] Priya: for EU-only logs: can exports be region-restricted and not leave eu?

[02:18] Carlos: for Private deployments, logs never leave the VPC unless you explicitly configure offsite export. For Hosted, we support region pinning (eu-central) and we can export directly to a eu S3 bucket using an EU endpoint. For strict data residency we recommend Redwood Private with our control-plane in your VPC or the on-prem bundle.

[02:36] Evan: ok about exports — real-time vs batch. We prefer pushing events to our SIEM in near real-time (splunk) but also want daily bulk exports for long-term archival. what ingestion options do you support?

[02:48] Carlos: we have three primary paths: 1) Streaming webhooks / syslog for near-real time (we support TLS and mutual TLS for syslog over tcp), 2) Managed push to customer S3 in NDJSON or gzipped batches on a schedule, and 3) direct SIEM connectors such as an SQS -> Splunk HTTP Event Collector pipeline that customers can wire up. For syslog you can point to your ingest endpoint; for S3 we support SSE-KMS and SSE-S3.

[03:18] Priya: BYOK — we need to use our KMS (AWS KMS with HSM backing) for encryption of logs in the bucket. can Redwood write encrypted to our key?

[03:25] Maya: yes we support BYOK for S3 exports — you provide the KMS key arn and we write objects with SSE-KMS using your key. For hosted storage at rest we use our own KMS, but we support envelope encryption and key wrapping for enterprise customers if BYOK is required. For Private deployments you can configure local KMS/HSM integration.

[03:45] Lena: rotation and access — who can decrypt? we need separation of duties.

[03:50] Carlos: when using customer-managed KMS, Redwood never has the plaintext access without an explicit cross-account grant. The S3 objects are encrypted with your key; you control key policies and rotation. For hosted-managed KMS we can provide audit logs showing which Redwood service principal performed the encryption operations.

[04:07] Evan: in a scenario where we do S3 export + Splunk ingestion, will you write a manifest file per batch to help our pipeline validate completeness?

[04:14] Carlos: yes each batch includes a manifest (NDJSON listing, object keys, record counts, checksums). we also sign manifests with an HMAC and provide a verification header.

[04:25] Priya: can we filter admin events? we don't want trivial events like token refresh flooding our SIEM. we want role-change, key-rotation, policy change, tenant-level exports, and failed auth attempts.

[04:34] Carlos: absolutely. export filters are configurable. default severity filtering is info/warn/error, but you can also define event categories to include/exclude. We also support sampling for high-volume request logs while sending all admin-level events.

[04:50] Maya: quick note on legal hold — if faced with litigation we can pin retention on specific workspaces and prevent purge. that can be a contract addendum for hosted customers.

[04:58] Lena: ok good. about the schema — do you have a published spec? Evan will want to map fields for SIEM parsers.

[05:04] Carlos: yes we have an event schema spec. i'll attach a sample NDJSON file to the follow-up. example fields: event_type, event_id, occurred_at, actor_id, actor_email, actor_roles, action, resource_id, resource_type, ip, geo, user_agent, outcome, change_set (list of changed attributes), context (kv), request_trace, source_cluster. Sorry the naming in some old docs is inconsistent (eventId vs event_id) — we recently standardized to snake_case.

[05:34] Evan: is there a way to correlate admin logs with model inference logs? say we want to know if a model rollout was happening when a spike occurred.

[05:41] Carlos: yes we emit a trace id for cross-service correlation. Model runtime emits the same trace when it is triggered by a config change. we also include the model variant id and the sequence length distribution snippet (small summary) — not full payloads.

[06:02] Priya: encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for webhook streaming?

[06:06] Maya: yes mTLS supported, TLS 1.2+; we also support client cert rotation. For syslog over TCP we recommend mTLS + mutual auth.

[06:15] Evan: audit log tamper-evidence — can we get hashes or Write-Once storage?

[06:20] Carlos: manifests include checksums; for stronger tamper resistance we can push manifests to your blockchain or to an append-only audit store (we offer integration with AWS QLDB on request). For hosted customers we maintain internal immutability controls and retention locks as part of SOC2 processes.

[06:40] Priya: what about admin UI events — console clicks like deleting a resource — are those captured as admin events?

[06:47] Carlos: yes meta events from the console are captured as admin_activity events (actor id, action, target). we also include the console session id and a short click-path string. We do not capture visual screenshots.

[07:01] Lena: any caveats around private keys for service accounts? where are they logged?

[07:06] Carlos: private keys are never logged. creation and rotation events are logged (who created, when), but the secret material is never recorded. we log the key fingerprint and reference id.

[07:18] Priya: retention costs — can you ballpark storage cost for NDJSON admin logs at our scale: ~200k admin events / month, avg event ~1.2KB?

[07:27] Maya: quick calc: 200k * 1.2KB ~= 240MB/month raw, compresses 4x gz so ~60MB. For 1 year that's ~720MB. Minimal, but index/search cost in Splunk/SIEM might add. We'll send a short spreadsheet with cold vs hot pricing.

[07:48] Evan: about exports for compliance — do you support pre-signed URLs for on-demand pull of archived exports?

[07:53] Carlos: yes you can use pre-signed S3 URLs with short TTL or we can create a secure transfer job and push to your SFTP.

[08:05] Priya: any PII scanning? can we request automatic redaction of user emails in logs?

[08:11] Carlos: we support configurable redaction rules at export time — you can mask or tokenise emails, user identifiers, and IPs. masking is applied just to the exported object if you choose; raw logs in your own S3 (if BYOK) remain under your control.

[08:26] Maya: on SOC 2 evidence collection — for auditor requests we can provide time-bound snapshots and an activity timeline. we'll include attestations in our SOC2 bundle.

[08:35] Priya: what's your process for responding to audit evidence requests?

[08:40] Maya: typically AE + SE + CSM coordinate: we provision a secure link, provide the requested logs/manifests, and a controls narrative. we try to respond within 3-5 business days depending on scope.

[08:52] Evan: question — if we do Redwood Private and host the control plane in our VPC, do you still keep any metadata in your control plane?

[08:59] Carlos: with Private with full air-gapped mode, no customer metadata is sent to Redwood control plane. If you choose a hybrid private mode, minimal telemetry for billing and health checks can be optionally shared; everything else stays on-prem.

[09:16] Lena: do you have SOC2 scope — does it include logging and change management?

[09:20] Maya: yes our SOC2 scope includes change management, access control, and logging. we will share the SOC2 Type II report and the controls mapping.

[09:27] Priya: on-format question: NDJSON vs CEF. Our SIEM expects CEF for some ingestion. do you output CEF?

[09:34] Carlos: we can emit NDJSON natively and provide a conversion layer to CEF or Common Event Format on the push side. we also support syslog which many SIEMs can parse into CEF.

[09:50] Evan: are event timestamps in UTC only or do you include timezone?

[09:54] Carlos: timestamps are RFC3339 with timezone offsets; we recommend normalising to UTC in the SIEM ingestion rules.

[10:02] Priya: any gotchas for retention in EU — e.g., cross-account replication to US?

[10:08] Carlos: replication is opt-in. we will not replicate EU exports to US unless explicitly configured. for hosted we can restrict S3 export endpoints to region.

[10:20] Maya: quick demo — Carlos will show a sample NDJSON export and the manifest in the shared screen. (screen share)

[10:30] Carlos: reading snippet: {"event_type":"admin_activity","event_id":"evt-9a3f","occurred_at":"2025-09-01T11:22:33Z","actor_email":"p.nair@tidewater.com","action":"change_role","resource_type":"workspace","resource_id":"ws-47","change_set": [{"field":"role","old":"viewer","new":"admin"}],"request_trace":"trc-xxx"} (this is sample, we redact actual email in the share)

[11:05] Priya: looks good. couple of notes: we'll need actor_email masked for exported copies to our security team. internal raw bucket may keep full emails under our BYOK key but viewers should see masked.

[11:15] Carlos: that's doable — masking at export layer yes.

[11:22] Evan: about the manifest HMAC, what key is used to sign?

[11:26] Carlos: we sign with a customer-shared secret or an ephemeral key exchange per job. if you want us to sign with your KMS signing key via kms:Sign we can integrate that too.

[11:38] Priya: uptime of export jobs — how do you handle failed pushes?

[11:42] Carlos: we have retry with exponential backoff and DLQ. failed batches go to a retry queue; if persistent failure we create a ticket to the customer. we keep the manifests for forensic review.

[11:55] Maya: ok summarise next steps — we'll send SOC2 + ISO, Carlos will drop a sample NDJSON to your S3 (we'll need an upload role) and we'll put together a cost spreadsheet. any other asks?

[12:04] Priya: also include the legal hold process in writing and a sample manifest with checksum example.

[12:09] Lena: and the redaction configuration doc.

[12:14] Maya: sure. we'll follow up. thanks everyone.

[12:20] (crosstalk / wrap up)

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps and some product names were mis-read by auto-transcribe (Redwood Dedicated appeared as Redwood Dedicate in one slide). Natural speech artifacts left intact.
